'''Christian Eyenga Moenge''' (born June 22, 1989) is a Congolese former professional [[basketball]] player. Eyenga was drafted by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] with the 30th pick in that year's [[2009 NBA draft]]. When drafted, he played for the [[LEB Plata|Spanish Third Division]] club [[CB Prat|Prat]], an affiliate of the [[Liga ACB|ACB]] club [[DKV Joventut]].

==Professional career==

===NBA career===
Eyenga played the 2010 [[NBA Summer League]] for the Cleveland Cavaliers. After that, he officially signed a two-year contract with the Cavaliers on July 23, 2010. He signed for $2 million over two years, with years three and four being options.<ref>[http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2010/6/28/1540775/nba-summer-league-rosters-vegas NBA Summer League Rosters - Vegas]</ref> On November 18, Eyenga was sent to the Cavaliers' [[NBA Development League]] affiliate, the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2010/news/11/18/cavs-eyenga.ap/index.html Cavs send rookie swingman Eyenga to NBA D-League]</ref> On January 2, he was recalled by the Cavs<ref>[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/eyenga_110102.html Cavaliers Recall Eyenga from BayHawks]</ref> and made his debut on the same day, against the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. He scored 4 points and grabbed 3 rebounds.

On March 15, 2012, Eyenga was traded along with [[Ramon Sessions]] to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for a protected first-round pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]], [[Jason Kapono]] and [[Luke Walton]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Lakers Acquire Ramon Sessions & Christian Eyenga | url = http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers_acquire_ramon_sessions__2012_03_15.html | work = NBA.com | date = 2012-03-15 | access-date = 2012-03-15}}</ref>

On August 10, 2012, Eyenga was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Denton: Magic Trade Howard in Four-Team Blockbuster | url = http://www.nba.com/magic/news/denton-magic-trade-howard-four-team-blockbuster | work = NBA.com | date = 2012-08-10 | access-date = 2012-08-10}}</ref>

On October 23, 2012, Eyenga was waived by the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-eyenga-johnson Magic Waive Eyenga, A. Johnson]</ref> He was then drafted by the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA D-League]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2012/index.html |title=2012 NBA D-League Draft |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2012-11-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105044827/http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2012/index.html |archive-date=2012-11-05 |url-status = dead }}</ref> On January 4, 2013, Eyenga was released by the Legends so he could sign in China.<ref>[http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2013/01/christian-eyenga-leaving-d-league-for-china.html Christian Eyenga Leaving D-League For China]</ref> In February 2013, he re-joined the Legends after a month in China.

===Overseas career===
In October 2011 he signed to play for [[Joventut Badalona]] in Spain during the [[2011 NBA lockout]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/32088/christian_eyenga_inks_with_fiatc_joventut_badalona_during_nba_lockout.html Christian Eyenga inks with FIATC Joventut Badalona during NBA lockout]</ref>

In January 2013, he signed with Shanxi Zhongyu of China.<ref>[http://www.niubball.com/2013/01/eyenga-replaces-williams-in-shanxi-mccants-on-the-way-out-in-foshan/ Eyenga replaces Williams in Shanxi; McCants on the way out in Foshan?]</ref><ref>[http://cbadata.sports.sohu.com/players/statistics/501568 CBA Profile]</ref> He left the same month and returned to America.

On July 25, 2013, Eyenga moved to Poland and signed with [[Basket Zielona Góra|Stelmet Zielona Góra]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Stelmet Zielona Gora announced Brackins, Robinson and Eyenga|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/poland/60216/stelmet-zielona-gora-announced-brackins-robinson-and-eyenga.html|publisher=Sportando.net|access-date=25 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130729200348/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/poland/60216/stelmet-zielona-gora-announced-brackins-robinson-and-eyenga.html|archive-date=29 July 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> On August 4, 2014, he signed a one-year deal with another Polish team [[Turów Zgorzelec]].<ref>{{cite news|title=PGE Turow tabs forward Eyenga|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/139986|access-date=4 August 2014|work=Euroleague.net}}</ref> In September 2014, Eyenga has been waived by the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=PGE Turow announces Mardy Collins|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/140932/180/pge-turow-announces-mardy-collins|access-date=5 November 2014|work=euroleague.net|issue=26 September 2014}}</ref> On November 12, 2014, he signed a one-season contract with the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]] team [[Pallacanestro Varese]].<ref>{{cite news|title=CHRISTIAN EYENGA NUOVA FIRMA PER LA OPENJOBMETIS|url=http://pallacanestrovarese.it/news/comunicati-stampa/4127-christian-eyenga-nuova-firma-per-la-openjobmetis.html|access-date=12 November 2014|work=pallacanestrovarese.it|language=it|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141112224037/http://pallacanestrovarese.it/news/comunicati-stampa/4127-christian-eyenga-nuova-firma-per-la-openjobmetis.html|archive-date=12 November 2014}}</ref>

On July 10, 2015, he signed with champions of Italy, [[Dinamo Sassari]] for the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=In casa Dinamo arriva Christian Eyenga|url=http://www.dinamobasket.com/sites/default/files/comunicati/Comunicato%20stampa%20n.%2002%20del%2010.7.2015_In%20casa%20Dinamo%20arriva%20Christian%20Eyenga_0.pdf|access-date=31 July 2015|work=Dinamobasket.com|date=10 July 2015|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Dinamo Sassari brings on high-flying Eyenga|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/66vn8utlh5nw4l7j/dinamo-sassari-brings-on-high-flying-eyenga|access-date=31 July 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=10 July 2015}}</ref> On February 5, 2016, he left Dinamo Sassari,<ref>{{cite news|title=Christian Eyenga saluta Sassari|url=http://www.dinamobasket.com/it/blog/christian-eyenga-saluta-sassari|date=5 February 2016|work=Dinamobasket.com|language=it}}</ref> and signed with [[Auxilium CUS Torino]] for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/190056/manital-torino-announces-christian-eyenga.html Manital Torino announces Christian Eyenga]</ref>

On August 16, 2016, Eyenga signed with Pallacanestro Varese for the 2016–17 season.<ref>[http://www.pallacanestrovarese.it/christian-eyenga-torna-alla-pallacanestro-varese/ CHRISTIAN EYENGA TORNA ALLA PALLACANESTRO VARESE] {{in lang|it}}</ref> On May 14, 2017, he signed with Spanish club [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja]] for the rest of the [[2016–17 ACB season]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/234485/unicaja-malaga-signs-christian-eyenga.html Unicaja Malaga signs Christian Eyenga]</ref>

On July 23, 2017, Eyenga signed with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]] for the [[2017–18 ACB season]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/242101/fuenlabrada-signs-christian-eyenga.html Fuenlabrada signs Christian Eyenga]</ref> At the end of the season Eyenga won the league award for [[ACB Most Spectacular Player]].

He averaged 9.4 points and 3.9 rebounds per game during the 2019–20 season. On August 4, 2020, Eyenga re-signed with the team.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fuenlabrada confirms Christian Eyenga |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/fuenlabrada-confirms-christian-eyenga/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 4, 2020 |date=August 4, 2020|last1=Borghesan |first1=Ennio Terrasi }}</ref> He signed a two-year deal with the team on July 3, 3021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Christian Eyenga officially re-signs with Urbas Fuenlabrada |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/christian-eyenga-officially-re-signs-with-urbas-fuenlabrada/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 3, 2021 |date=July 3, 2021|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }}</ref>

On November 12, 2023, he signed with [[Lille Métropole BC|Lille Métropole]] of the [[LNB Pro B]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/christian-eyenga-signs-with-lille-metropole-bc/|title=Christian Eyenga signs with Lille Metropole BC|last=|first=|date=November 12, 2023|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=November 12, 2023}}</ref>

==DR Congo national team==
Eyenga often represents the [[DR Congo national basketball team]] at international tournaments. At the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification]], he averaged 14.7 points, 7.0 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game.
